title: SEO basics for a site
when: The user wants a site to show up and look good in search results and link previews.
inputs: the words people would search for
prompt:
Goal: Each page has a unique, descriptive title and description, clean headings, crawlable links and preview tags.
Steps:
1. Pick one main search phrase per page from the words of the audience (bakery in Porto, not artisanal experiences).
2. Write a unique <title> of 50 to 60 characters: page topic first, site name last.
3. Write a meta description of 120 to 160 characters that says what the page offers and invites a click.
4. Use one h1 that matches the topic, h2 for sections, descriptive link text, and alt text on meaningful images.
5. Add og:title, og:description, og:image and a canonical link with the final URL when it is known.
6. Keep URLs and file names short and readable (pricing.html, not page2.html).
Quality bar:
- No two pages share a title or description.
- Copy is written for people, with the phrase used naturally.
- Every page is reachable through a normal link.
Pitfalls:
- Keyword stuffing.
- Content only inside images or loaded by script after interaction.
- Same title on all pages.
Verify:
- [ ] Each page has title, description, lang and one h1.
- [ ] Description length is 50 to 160 characters.
- [ ] Open graph tags exist.
- [ ] Links use real text.
Output: Updated head sections and headings for every page, plus a short list of the target phrase per page.

examples.input: melhore o SEO do site da minha clínica
examples.output: titles like "Physiotherapy in Campinas | Clinica Movimento", unique descriptions, og tags on 5 pages
